claims.text: A vendor evaluation checks each candidate against criteria taken from the team's own requirements and risks, written down before looking at the candidates; criteria written afterwards tend to follow the favourite's strengths.
claims.source_hint: Outline item 1; misconception 3; payment-gateway-evaluation.md @ stage-3 lines 8-13

claims.text: YC-9: an order is never refunded twice, even when sending to the gateway must be retried. The requirements' open questions include whether bank transfer orders can be refunded through the gateway.

Risk R1: the gateway's refund API may behave differently from its documentation, rated high likelihood and high impact. R2: the gateway may not accept an idempotency key, so a resend could refund twice. R4's response: customer care handles refused refunds by hand.

A candidate failing a knock-out criterion is out, so price or features cannot make up for it; failing another criterion is a cost to plan around. A trial shows what the system does, documentation what the vendor wrote; because of R1 each criterion is decided by the trial call.

Criteria from refund-requirements.md or risk register, not vendor material; knock-out ('Loại ngay') failure rules out before comparing anything, price included. T1 from YC-9, R2; T2 from R1 and design step 6 (changes if result comes by callback); T4, T5 from open questions; only T1, T3 knock-out.

Results: each criterion tried by a real call because of R1. T1: B's docs do not mention it, two sends made two refunds. T3: B's recorded as met, but error codes differ from docs in two calls. A fails T4. B ruled out at T1; its other rows kept so a later evaluation need not retry.
The open question on bank transfers is closed: with Gateway A they are refused and customer care handles them by hand, as for R4.

Beyond features: A answered two technical questions within the day, someone could read call logs; B answered after three days with a link to docs. A has a change page per API version and emails registered engineers; B posts on its home page. Team lives with both for years.

ADR 0010 chooses Gateway A; B ruled out at T1 (R2) because a resend after a network error could refund twice, against YC-9; it points to the evaluation for criteria, results, SLA and contract terms instead of repeating them.
Every figure about the two gateways is assumed for illustration, not from a real vendor; the evaluation happened in the first week of Sprint 15, before the refund-sending job was written.
Try it: a candidate with no test environment fails T3, a knock-out criterion, before price or features are compared; T3 fails outright; T1 cannot be checked without a test environment.
The refund saga step resends with the same idempotency key after no answer, which is why T1 is knock-out.
ADR 0010's exit plan starts by choosing a new gateway through an evaluation like payment-gateway-evaluation.md, with the same criteria.
